reviews.text: Excellent service and attitude
Good place, top-notch doctors, especially the cardiologist Fernando, who is very experienced and excellent.

Terrible service. They had my dog ​​there and couldn't diagnose him; they're just interested in making money. My dog ​​was already in very bad shape with his kidneys and they didn't realize it. What kind of doctors do they have?
Excellent service, friendly

Luka arrived at the vet with terrible diarrhea. He was seen immediately, if not right away, then within a reasonable time. He was dehydrated, and Dr. Cynthia examined him and diagnosed severe dehydration. He had to stay hospitalized for two days. They found a parasite, prescribed medication, and he's as good as new.
Excellent service. Other vets might be cheaper, but they're not effective, I can attest to that.
Terrible service, they refuse to treat pets in emergency cases.

I was recommended this place because they have the equipment to handle almost any case and offer specialties, a place for emergencies and serious cases. HOWEVER, their patient management is not transparent. THEY NEVER GIVE YOU THE RESULTS OF MEDICAL EXAMS; they pass the buck between doctors and reception, treating you like a fool by just stalling or saying they'll send them by email, which they never do. This lack of transparency allows them to hide mismanagement. I keep my pets' medical records, and while they were being treated there, I DID NOT RECEIVE A SINGLE MEDICAL STUDY. You only receive them if you pay as an external service; if they do the treatment themselves, THEY GIVE YOU NOTHING BUT CHARGE YOU FOR EVERYTHING. I recommend going there for medical exams, not for bringing your pets because they won't let you know anything, even with the paperwork in hand.
I loved it, but it's hard to find the place; it's missing a sign.
With one of my little ones, we struggled to get the necessary tests and specialist consultations done. Due to an emergency, we found this place and received all the services immediately.
I thought it was good, but the studio prices were very expensive.

The hospital has a lot of equipment and the care for the dogs is humane. However, it's also expensive and very disorganized. My dog ​​passed away, and they let me choose the urn and promised me a print of her paw prints and fur. When I arrived for the ashes, they only gave me the urn, and I had to remind them about the rest. I didn't receive the urn I ordered; the supposed paw prints were just hastily stamped on some random white paper in an unmarked envelope, and they lost the fur. They kept me waiting for an hour for nothing. While that was happening, a man was complaining that they wanted to charge him for a test he hadn't authorized and that hadn't been charged to the original account. It's clear they're a mess.
If you have an emergency, go, but stay in control of the situation and monitor every step of the process. If your dog dies and you want their fur, cut it yourself when you say goodbye. If you can, bring epoxy putty and use it to make the paw print. I didn't want to witness the cremation, which is why I didn't pay for the package to be present, but after seeing the mess they make, I suggest you pay for it and be present, lest they give you the ashes of another dog.

Terrible service, we waited for over an hour and they didn't attend to us. The argument when we approached reception to ask was that they only handle emergencies, and of course, if I'm there at 11 pm with my dog ​​in critical condition, I think that's an emergency.
Empathetic, very good service
Excellent service!!
The specialists' work is good, but the service is TERRIBLE.

Good hospital.

I've been taking my dogs to this veterinary hospital for many years, and overall, my experience has always been very good. It's a place I trust and would return to without hesitation.

My dogs have been hospitalized on several occasions and have always received excellent care. What speaks volumes to me is seeing them leave after being hospitalized: calm, well cared for, and without the stress one would expect after a hospital stay.

We've also had several emergency situations, and they've always responded quickly. In moments like these, having a hospital where you know they'll take care of you and act swiftly provides immense peace of mind. On several occasions, they've managed to save my dogs and help us through very difficult situations.

Unfortunately, on one occasion, due to the health condition of one of my dogs, we had to make the difficult decision to euthanize him. Despite the painful moment, we received very humane, respectful, and empathetic care, something I will always be grateful for.

I want to especially highlight the care provided by Dr. Alfonso, Dr. Fernando, and Dr. Itzel, who have been excellent professionals and have given me a level of care that has inspired great confidence.

I also previously received care from ophthalmologist Dr. Ramírez, whose care I found excellent. My most recent experience with Dr. Diana, however, was not the same and was not to my liking; I feel I had previously received much better care in this area.

The only point for improvement I would suggest is that the reception staff could be friendlier. The previous receptionists were excellent, very attentive, and friendly.

Aside from these details, my experience over all these years has been good. I haven't had any major problems, and I consider it a reliable hospital with good care and, above all, a team that has responded well and helped my dogs recover in emergencies.
The service is always friendly; they operated on my baby for a tumor and are continuing the treatment according to the letter. It's open 24 hours a day.
I arrived with my cat in an emergency, possibly needing surgery, and waited over an hour for treatment. This establishment is not for medical emergencies.
Excellent doctors and their care. Empathetic and professional.
Good service and explanation
Excellent service

Highly recommended! Here you'll find expert doctors and staff with an excellent attitude and helpfulness. The place is super clean and well-ventilated, which is VERY important to prevent the spread of germs to other pets 😄
I had a baby kitten admitted there and she did very well.
Very humane treatment of my dog. Patience and gentleness. The staff were very kind, attentive, and friendly.

TERRIBLE HOSPITAL. We took our dog for a biopsy, and it turns out she was in bad shape from the moment she left the lab. It's unbelievable that for over three weeks the so-called oncologist didn't realize she had contracted pneumonia. We brought videos, photos, everything for them to evaluate her, and it turns out that only when she was extremely ill did they realize it was pneumonia. Several doctors examined her, and no one noticed. It was truly a joke. We paid for all the tests they ordered, and NONE OF THEM NOTICED. Our dog's death was due to NEGLIGENCE. DO NOT GO TO THAT HOSPITAL.

Today I went for a consultation, and I highly recommend this branch. They not only followed up with my kitten, but they also stabilized her and gave me the time to examine her with all the patience in the world 🌎
They used pheromones to keep her calm.
Excellent service, bravo! ❤️

Terrible service. We went there because my dog ​​had been very ill. They never told us what was wrong with him; he was very sick. He was used to being with us, and we thought they would be able to help him. They did nothing. Dr. Guadalupe kept telling us it was something wrong with his head, that we needed tests to see if he had a tumor or something. They kept ordering test after test, but they never gave us the correct results. They sent us for a medication that could help him a lot, and the doctor told us we could get it at any pharmacy, that it was very easy. We spent an hour looking for it at the pharmacies he told us about, and they didn't have it. We decided to take our dog out of there because they never told us what was wrong with him or anything. They charged us for cans of food that were never given to the dog. If you're going to this hospital, I don't recommend it because he had more problems later on, and they never offered any solutions or progress. When we went to pick up our pet, the doctor took him downstairs and gave him to us and just said, "In the end, I never knew what he had," and laughed. We went to another vet, and they immediately told us he had a stomach infection, nothing to do with his head. We were given the bad news that there was a 50/50 chance of survival, and sadly my dog ​​passed away at only 3 years old.

Dr. José Guadalupe is inhumane. Out of nowhere, without even examining him, he wanted to euthanize a kitten.
TERRIBLE SERVICE!
Don't go there!

The visit was for an ultrasound, the service was good, there was only one issue with the medical history that they already had but couldn't see, it was resolved quickly and the service and delivery of the results was fast even though there was a high volume of patients.

A great place to take your pets, with excellent service and treatment for both animals and owners.
Highly recommend taking your pet here.

My rating for them... ZERO. They're only interested in the money for tests and consultations, but they couldn't care less about follow-up for any chronic illness they don't understand. They sent me home saying that small breed dogs tend to get hemorrhagic gastroenteritis. The so-called gastroenterologist never saw me again and just told me to continue with the hydrolyzed diet, nothing more; even though my dog ​​was still vomiting daily, had diarrhea, and blood in her stool. Obviously, I hate them, which is why I'm sharing this :)

I think it's despicable that they profit from the lives of living beings there. I took my sick dog to get checked out, and they told me he needed to stay there and that they had to perform a procedure at another clinic. It turns out that the other clinic couldn't do anything because all four of his paws were severely injured; he was covered in bites and stab wounds. And then, when I took him to another clinic, they told me they had only sedated him and that was it. The doctor explained that they didn't have to do that and that it wasn't necessary for him to be hospitalized. It's obvious they're just doing it to make more and more money. I think it's despicable that they do that kind of thing.

TERRIBLE PLACE!!!! This place presents itself as specialists, but they're only specialists in taking your money!! We took our dogs here, and unfortunately, they started a treatment on one of our dogs that ended up costing over $120,000 pesos, and in the end, due to medical negligence, they returned our dog to us dead! I hope places like this, which only seek to profit from the love people have for their pets, are shut down soon! It's a shame we ended up in this place and trusted their doctors!

I went to them because of an emergency with my dog ​​😢. It's easy to get to. It's a very nice house with a tree in the center, protected inside the house, which provides peace and quiet while you wait. The doctors and reception staff are excellent. Thank you. Dr. Samantha and her colleague were the ones who received my little one. Thank you.
Its main advantage is 24-hour service, however, it can be slow. Also consider that the costs may not be affordable for everyone.

Terrible service. I took my dog ​​in for a checkup because she had an injured paw. When we arrived, we told the vet why she was there and that my dog ​​has a heart condition, which is exacerbated by the pain and anxiety of being at the vet. She completely ignored us. They kept us waiting for an hour and twenty minutes, with no one at reception and no way to leave because the doors are electric and only they control them. I had to call while I was inside to ask if they would see us and if not, to have someone come out and let us in. The person who answered was very rude and told us that "if we had to wait another half hour, maybe they would see us"... I absolutely do not recommend this place.

My experience with this clinic ended up being very disappointing.

I decided to take my dog ​​there because Dr. Jorge was recommended to me, and I must say his care was excellent. He made a good diagnosis, clearly explained the treatment, and told us that we only needed to come in for a check-up every six months. The rest of the time, we just had to pick up the monthly prescription for the medication.

From that moment on, the problems with the administrative department began. Month after month, the prescription was delivered with errors: incorrect dates, incomplete information, or data entered incorrectly, which caused the pharmacy to reject it, and we had to return to have it corrected. It's unbelievable that such a simple procedure could never be done correctly.

In March, we went for the scheduled check-up, all the requested tests were performed, and we paid the bill in full without any problems. Even so, they didn't even send us the test results until we requested them by email.

Later, we were informed that Dr. Jorge no longer worked there and were required to bring my dog ​​back for another appointment, even though they had his complete medical record and he had only been seen a few weeks prior. When we explained that we couldn't afford to pay for it again so soon, the response was that "this time" they would do us the favor of giving us the medication. Finally, Dr. Gabriela authorized them to maintain the previously established follow-up schedule and allowed us to continue picking up only the prescription until the next six-month check-up.

However, weeks later, the exact same thing happened again. We were informed that Dr. Gabriela no longer worked at the clinic either, and again they tried to force us to pay for another appointment to obtain a prescription for a treatment that was already indicated and documented in his file.

To make matters worse, the prescription was once again incorrectly written. When we requested a correction, the reception staff's attitude was completely inappropriate. They made us wait without saying how long it would take, showed obvious annoyance at having to correct a mistake they themselves had made, and when they finally gave us the new prescription, the treatment was so discourteous that it was clear they had little interest in providing professional care.

It's a shame, because the veterinarians who treated my pet proved to be good professionals. Unfortunately, disorganized administrative services, constant errors, changes in criteria, and disrespectful treatment made the entire experience very negative.

I would not entrust my pet's care to this place again, nor would I recommend it. The quality of a clinic doesn't depend solely on its veterinarians; it also depends on the organization and the respect with which they treat their clients.
Excellent treatment of my pet and me

I loved the service! We arrived early, before our appointment, and were seen on time even though it was packed.
And Dolly's checkup went wonderfully. I highly recommend it!
Very clean. With service available at all hours and most specialties.

Terrible service. We arrived because our dog needed an emergency, and when we got there, the examination room was empty (no patients). The receptionists told us the doctors were making their rounds and to wait a bit; however, more than an hour passed, and we were never seen.

When we told them we were leaving to find another hospital, the receptionists didn't care. We absolutely do not recommend this place, supposedly for emergencies.

This is the second time we've been to this hospital. The care is excellent; they treated our kitten with great care and patience. They explained the necessary care, feeding, and that we could come back if any complications arose.

I have complete confidence in the staff, who are very kind and clearly experienced. I wholeheartedly recommend bringing your pets here if you need immediate attention.

I went to Pet&Vet Ciudad Jardín for an emergency with my pet and left with the feeling that the order of priorities was backwards.

In a situation where you expect the basics—immediate attention, stabilization, and pain relief—the first thing I received was a breakdown of costs and options. Lots of paperwork, many alternatives, little clinical progress in those minutes that, for someone bringing their pet in for an emergency, feel like an eternity.

I perfectly understand that a veterinary hospital needs to work with clear budgets and that medical care has costs. That's not up for debate. What did make me uncomfortable was the feeling that the financial discussion took the place that should normally be occupied by the initial care of the patient. In an emergency, instinct expects to see hands acting before calculators.

The impression I got is that the approach could be greatly improved if the priority in critical cases were to stabilize first and explain costs later, without interrupting urgent basic care. Because when you arrive with a suffering dog, you're not thinking about "premium or standard options," you're thinking about ending their suffering.

It was recommended to me as a good place, and I went there with confidence. That's why the contrast was so stark. I don't doubt their medical skills, but the experience in the emergency room can completely shape one's perception of the service.
I hope they reconsider, because a veterinary hospital isn't only measured by what it can do, but by how it responds in the first minute when an animal arrives vulnerable. And that's precisely where the most care is needed. I'm sorry, but being good doctors is useless if attention and empathy are a crucial part of the process. I don't recommend them, and I will never go back to this place.

Terrible experience. I DO NOT RECOMMEND IT.

A few weeks ago, I arrived around 12:30 a.m. because my cat stopped breathing for a few moments. Although she regained consciousness, I decided to take her in immediately because she had never experienced anything like that before, and like anyone, I was very worried.

From the moment I arrived, the service seemed quite poor. The doctor tried to measure her heart rate with a device that didn't even work, so he ended up counting the beats manually and with the heart rate monitor (Okai). He initially told me that the heart rate was slightly below normal, although "normal" was a bit of a stretch, meaning I was reassured. After asking me countless questions to complete his paperwork and several back-and-forths that lengthened the entire process, I ended up spending almost three hours there.

Later, he told me that the head of the department, Dr. Areli Cervantes, would explain the recommended tests and procedures. The breakdown included tests for feline leukemia and FIV, oxygen, and X-rays. I didn't understand—why were they a priority at that moment? And if they truly considered it a respiratory emergency, why didn't they administer oxygen during the almost three hours we were there? Other tests I saw there seemed appropriate. By the way, they billed me 2,000 pesos as a deposit for materials, and some people say they keep it.

Regarding the electrocardiogram, they told me it would have to be the next day and only if there was availability. That also seemed strange to me, considering I went to a veterinary hospital for an emergency. I also didn't receive a clear explanation about what they were looking for in the X-rays or what information they would provide.

What worried me most was their insistence on hospitalizing her. They asked me to keep her admitted when they couldn't even guarantee that the electrocardiogram would be performed the next day.

As for the doctor's attitude, I honestly found her lacking in empathy. When I questioned the preliminary diagnosis and asked for explanations about the suggested tests, I received responses that were passive-aggressively arrogant, though not exaggerated. She mentioned a possible heart murmur, that my kitten was moving a lot/her heart rate was significantly higher than normal, and various scenarios that, far from clarifying my doubts, only increased my anxiety. She even insisted that if anything happened again, they had resuscitation equipment and that if I decided to take her home, it would be entirely my responsibility. Rather than guiding me, she made me feel guilty for questioning her.

Furthermore, the first doctor and the second doctor didn't seem to agree in their assessments, which only added to my uncertainty. The most frustrating thing is that, after this whole experience, no one explained specific care, follow-up options, priority tests, or concrete recommendations for my kitten. I left with practically more questions than when I arrived.

While I was there, a little dog arrived having seizures. Its owners were given a quote of around 15,000 pesos, but they ultimately decided against hospitalizing it because they weren't convinced either. From that moment on, I noticed a change in the doctor's attitude.

In the end, they make you sign a voluntary discharge form that gives the impression of completely absolving them of any responsibility. Added to everything else, it leaves a rather unpleasant feeling.

In conclusion: I wasn't bothered by the cost, nor did I expect them to resolve everything immediately. What I was looking for was emergency care, clear explanations, empathy, and trust. Unfortunately, I didn't find any of those things. We decided to follow our intuition and look for other options, and honestly, it was the best decision. When you arrive at a place like that, you do so worried, scared, and looking for help, not feeling judged or pressured. I took her to the Mexican Kennel Club, and the treatment was wonderful, and everything was great. My kitten doesn't have a breath sound... anyway, I do recommend this place.

Terrible experience. I went to the emergency room on Friday seeking the support of a specific specialist. The doctor who saw me said it wasn't necessary, even though tests done elsewhere indicated otherwise. I wasn't given any report of the consultation. Dr. Pamela was only concerned with judging the situation. I went for a medical opinion, not a moral one. There are better hospitals. I absolutely do not recommend this place.

I went because my trusted veterinarian asked me to see an orthopedist to confirm if my dog ​​had a ruptured tendon and, if so, to cover the cost of surgery. Previously, my veterinarian, suspecting a ruptured tendon, performed a "drawer test" on my dog. During this test, my dog ​​was sedated with inhaled anesthesia because it's a very painful procedure, and the more tense the muscle, the less accurate the test can be. When it came back positive, he asked me to find an orthopedist. In the end, the doctor who saw me was Dr. Alanis, who wasn't even an orthopedist, even though we had been very clear about requesting a consultation with one. I showed him a recording of my trusted veterinarian performing the drawer test on my dog, which came back positive, and I also showed him my dog's X-rays. The doctor took more x-rays, but he performed the same old test on my dog ​​without even telling us, and it only hurt her more. My dog ​​cried and walked away in worse shape. Finally, he told us that surgery with titanium plates and screws in her entire leg was necessary. I didn't like that solution, so I went to another veterinary hospital with a REAL ORTHOPEDIST, and the solution he gave us for my dog ​​was completely different. We asked for the x-rays, and they told us they would send them to us by email within half an hour to an hour at the most. We waited a week, trying to be patient, and they never sent anything. I had to ask again for the x-rays, and the response I got was that they had already sent them. I showed them that I hadn't received any email and mentioned that if they had sent them, I wouldn't be bothering to come back to ask for what I was entitled to. Luckily, they sent the x-rays immediately.
